videos.title: All properties: the group today
videos.intro: Across properties holds three screens that sit above any one hotel: All properties, Properties and People. This first video is All properties, for the owner and Admin.

scenes.say: Open All properties, under Across properties in the menu. Each property is shown on its own business date.
The dark panel is the group today: occupancy, average rate, RevPAR and room revenue, every property added up.
Under each figure, the month so far, and the same month last year.
Last year counts only the properties that sold a room in that month a year back. Here it reads 0 of 1, so the last year figures are a dash.
Needs you lists what to act on, at every property. A property whose business date is behind comes first.
Each line names the property and what is waiting, such as an arrival not yet checked in. Click it to open the screen that deals with it.
Below, there is a row for each property, with its business date. Click its name to open its Rooms.
Each figure shows today on top, and the month so far under it.
The last column compares this month's room revenue so far with the same month last year.
A property with nothing to compare says No last year yet.

videos.outro: A figure that did not come back is a dash, never a zero. And test hotels are never counted here.

videos.title: Properties: a card per property
videos.intro: Properties shows a card for each hotel. The owner sees more on it than everyone else. Here are both.

scenes.say: This is the owner's view. The line under the title counts the properties open, and any closed.
Each card shows the property's name and its code.
Then its rooms, its room types, and its G S T I N, which prints on every invoice. Under it, the G S T in use for rooms, the restaurant and the rest.
Open shows the property's own page, with its figures and its team.
Calendar switches to the property, and opens its Rooms screen.
Edit changes its details. The next video shows how.
Close takes a property out of every picker. Nothing is deleted, and Reopen brings it back. Close does not ask first.
While guests are checked in, Close is off, and the card says why.
Everyone else sees a simpler card. Here, the general manager's.
Only the properties you can reach are listed.
Each shows the check in and check out times.
And the G S T in use, one line for each kind.
Open the Calendar takes you into that property, on its Rooms screen.

videos.outro: Under each card, the owner can also make a test hotel: a practice copy of that hotel's setup, with no guests or money.

videos.title: Editing and adding a property
videos.intro: This video is for the owner: changing a property's details, and adding a new property.

scenes.say: On the property's card, click Edit. These details print on the property's invoices.
The code is shown, greyed out.
It is in every web address and every invoice number, so it cannot be changed.
Change the name, city, state, address, phone or email as needed.
The G S T I N is fifteen characters, the two-digit state code first.
Click Save. If something is wrong, the message says why, and nothing is saved.
To add a property, scroll down to Add a property.
Type its code, two to eight letters or digits. Choose it with care: it can never be changed.
Then its name and its city, and if you have them, its state and G S T I N.
Type the provisioning key, the key for this system. Being signed in is not enough on its own.
Click Create the property. The new property has its room types, but no rooms yet. Add its rooms next.

videos.outro: The rest of a property's profile, such as its PIN code and website, is kept in Settings.

videos.title: One property and its team
videos.intro: Each property has its own page, with its figures and the people who work there. The owner opens it with Open, on the property's card.

scenes.say: The first row is today: rooms sold, occupancy, rooms empty, and guests in house now.
The second is the month to date: room revenue, average rate, RevPAR, and the rooms the property has. A figure not measured yet is a dash.
The F S S A I licence number prints on food bills. The owner, an Admin or the GM clicks Change to type it.
Who works here lists everyone at this property, with their role.
Starts on is the first screen after they sign in: Dashboard, Rooms or Calendar. It saves as soon as you choose.
The key sets a new password for them.
Remove takes them off this property. It asks first, and their account stays.
To add somebody, click Add somebody here.
Type their name.
And the email they sign in with. A typo here means they cannot sign in at all.
Type a password for them, at least eight characters. It shows as you type, so you can read it back.
Choose what they do here.
Click Add. They can sign in straight away, and see this property only. Tell them the password yourself: nothing is emailed.

videos.outro: A GM or Admin can open their own property's page too. Anybody else is told it is not theirs to manage.

videos.title: People: everyone, and where they work
videos.intro: People lists everybody who can sign in: where they work, and as what. In this video you will read the list, take a property away, and switch somebody off.

scenes.say: Open People. The line under the title counts the people active, and how many reach every property.
A yellow note names anybody who can sign in and see nothing. Give them a property, or the system looks broken to them.
Every property marks a group administrator. They reach every property, including ones added later.
Everyone else has a chip for each property they work at, with their role there.
No property yet means this account opens empty.
Give a property fixes that. The next video shows how.
The cross on a chip takes that property away.
It asks first, naming who and where.
They can no longer work there. Their account stays, and their name stays on everything they did.
Click Remove, or Cancel.
Deactivate switches somebody off: they can no longer sign in. It does not ask first. Bring them back undoes it.

videos.outro: Nobody is ever deleted. Somebody who has left is switched off, so their name stays on everything they did.

videos.title: Adding somebody, and giving them a property
videos.intro: Access is given property by property. That is what stops one hotel seeing another's guests. Here is how to add somebody, as the owner and as the GM.

scenes.say: On People, click Add somebody.
Type their name.
And the email they will sign in with. A typo here means they cannot sign in at all.
Type a password for them, at least eight characters.
It is hidden. Show lets you read it back to them.
This adds an ordinary member of staff. Making somebody a group administrator, who reaches every property, takes the provisioning key.
Click Add. They can sign in now, but see nothing until they have a property.
So on their card, click Give a property, and choose which property.
Choose what they do there.
The line underneath says what that role does.
Click Give access.
A GM adds somebody at their own property, in one step. Where they work offers their own hotel.
Doing what offers every role but Owner and Admin.
They see this property only. Only the owner can make somebody an Admin.

videos.outro: A password for an Owner, Admin or GM is at least ten characters. Nothing is emailed: tell them the password and the address yourself.

videos.title: A new password, and a person's details
videos.intro: Somebody forgot their password, or their name is spelt wrong. In this video you will fix both, on People.

scenes.say: On their card, click Password.
The window names the person. Their old password stops working immediately.
Type the new one. They type it at a terminal in front of guests, so make it something they can remember.
Show lets you read it back.
It names the address they sign in with. Nothing is emailed: tell them yourself.
Click Set it.
To change a person's details, click Edit.
Correct their name. It is on everything they have done.
Add or change their phone.
Starts on chooses the first screen after they sign in. They can change it themselves.
Click Save. The email cannot be changed here: it is how they sign in.

videos.outro: That is Across properties. Thank you for watching.
